title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic 'analysis situs', a combinatorial or tame-topological framework. The ingredients are:
- a class M (or 𝓕) of 'figures';
- a partial order X ≤ Y, meaning X is a sub-figure of Y;
- for each figure F, a set F̃ (also written F̂) of distinguished sub-figures, called on the page 'multitubulaires' or similar (reading uncertain);
- a refinement relation F' ≪ F, think of subdivisions;
- restriction F'|X of a refinement of F to a sub-figure X;
- a Sup operation.

The axiom AR on p.67 (Axiome de recollement des raffinements) reads as follows. Suppose that for every X ∈ F̃ we are given a refinement F'_X ≪ X, and that these satisfy F'_Y = F'_X|Y whenever Y ≤ X. Then there is a refinement F' ≪ F with F'|X = F'_X for all X ∈ F̃.

First NB. The F' in AR is unique. Grothendieck names it 'the refinement of F obtained by gluing' (recollement) from the refinements F'_X of its distinguished sub-figures. This is a sheaf-type statement: the refinements of F correspond to compatible families of refinements over the poset F̃.

Second NB: the essential content of AR. The family F'_X must be mutually compatible, so that one can form F' = Sup_{X∈F̃} F'_X.
- When F̃ is finite, forming the Sup is no problem by itself.
- The real difficulty is comparing F'_X and F'_Y when X and Y are incomparable. The hypothesis of AR only controls comparable pairs.

The two-piece gluing statement. Hence he proposes a strengthened two-piece statement, labelled 'Conj (AR')' (the transcription's 'Contre-exemple (At W')' is a misreading). Let X, Y ∈ M be incomparable and T = X ∩ Y. Let X' ≪ X and Y' ≪ Y satisfy X'|T = Y'|T, or equivalently X'|Z = Y'|Z for all Z ∈ X̂ ∩ Ŷ. Then X' and Y' are compatible; the crossed symbol is a compatibility relation, not ≤.

What AR' buys. It is presented as a variant, 'barely weaker' (or barely modified), of AR.
- It implies AR at least when F̃ is finite.
- More generally, it yields the pairwise compatibility of the F'_X.
- Whenever Sup F'_X exists, that Sup is the required gluing; p.69 proves this.

So the page isolates the classical fact that subdivisions agreeing on an overlap can be united. For simplicial complexes: subdivisions of two subcomplexes that agree on the intersection unite to a subdivision of the union. The page proposes this as the basic axiom from which the general gluing axiom follows by finite induction.
errors: The transcribed conclusion 'X' ≤ Y'' cannot be right. X' refines X and Y' refines Y, so the intended relation must be 'compatible' (admitting a common refinement / Sup). This is a transcription issue, not Grothendieck's error.

Gap left open by Grothendieck: the equivalence 'X'|T = Y'|T iff X'|Z = Y'|Z for all Z ∈ X̂∩Ŷ' tacitly requires T = X∩Y to be a figure with T̂ = X̂∩Ŷ. Likewise, 'AR' implies AR for F̃ infinite' requires existence of the Sup, which he acknowledges.
The parenthetical claim that the Sup 'could be formed independently of the axiom if F̃ is finite' still presupposes pairwise compatibility. He immediately notes this, so it is not a real error.

ideas.what: Uniqueness and naming of the refinement obtained by gluing compatible refinements of the distinguished sub-figures
ideas.modern_name: sheaf/descent property of subdivisions (refinements form a sheaf on the poset of subfigures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in PL topology (e.g. Rourke–Sanderson); o-minimal cell decompositions (van den Dries)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is advocated in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) but without this axiomatics

ideas.what: Reduction of the general gluing axiom AR to a two-piece compatibility axiom AR' (agreement on X∩Y implies compatibility), sufficient for finite F̃
ideas.modern_name: Mayer–Vietoris / two-set gluing reduction for subdivisions; amalgamation property

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at an axiomatic 'tame topology' via figures, refinements and gluing axioms (AR, AR') remains unpublished. The question whether AR' should be an axiom or a theorem is left open (labelled 'Conj').
missed.quote: Conj (AR') : X, Y ∈ M avec X ≰ Y ... tels que X'|T = Y'|T ... Alors X' ≍ Y' !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of interest for comparisons with o-minimal structures and axiomatic approaches to tame topology. The specific content of this page is routine combinatorial topology.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technically routine page in an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology project: a gluing axiom for subdivisions and its reduction to the two-piece case. The project itself is historically interesting, but the page contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Contre-exemple (At W')' should most likely read 'Conj (AR')', i.e. a conjecture/strengthened axiom, not a counterexample.
'At W' throughout the page is most likely 'AR' (Axiome de recollement des raffinements, introduced on p.67).
'Donc la nécessité de At W est claire' is more likely something like 'D'où le renforcement de AR que voici', introducing AR'.
The conclusion 'X' ≤ Y'' should be a compatibility symbol (X' ≍ Y'), not ≤.
'à partir des raffinements F'_X (not F_X) de ses multi...' — the word 'multitubulaires' is uncertain.
